consequences: Each release attaches Disk-Usage.dmg under that exact name. The first make dmg on a machine asks to let the terminal control Finder.
context: Releases were a versioned zip that users unzipped, dragged to Applications and then cleared the quarantine flag on in Terminal.
decision: make dmg builds dist-release/Disk-Usage.dmg with tools/dmg/ (Finder-laid-out window: app, arrow, Applications, background rendered from background.html). The name carries no version so the README can link to releases/latest/download/Disk-Usage.dmg. make release-zip is removed; the README tells users to use Open Anyway, with xattr as the alternative.
title: Ship the app as a DMG installer instead of a zip

consequences: New source files need the header. Any lint warning fails make check.
context: The code had no linters and no per-file copyright notice. The app's About panel has no copyright line, so LICENSE is the only source of the notice.
decision: Every source file starts with 'Copyright (c) 2026 Wayne Davies' and an SPDX MIT identifier pointing at LICENSE. make lint runs cargo fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, ESLint (typescript-eslint recommendedTypeChecked plus react-hooks) and prettier --check; make check runs it first. Line width is 100 for both rustfmt and Prettier. strictTypeChecked was tried and dropped: it rejects numbers in template strings, which this code uses everywhere.
title: Lint and format with clippy, rustfmt, ESLint and Prettier; licence header on every source file

consequences: A folder scan never shows free space, and the switch's tooltip says so. The free block has no zoom, reveal or context menu.
context: Free space was asked for as a block in the treemap, on by default with a toggle that persists. Beside a single folder, a volume's free space dwarfs the folder and says nothing about it.
decision: The free-space block is added to the top-level layout only when the view is the scan root and the root is / or a disk under /Volumes. The toggle is a switch in the title bar, remembered in localStorage (a per-viewer UI preference; it defaults to on if storage is unavailable).
title: Free space drawn only at the top of a whole-volume scan

consequences: Uses the user's existing Claude sign-in; answers stream. Claude cannot inspect the disk itself and the app deletes nothing, so advice rests on names, paths and sizes. Chats are lost on relaunch. Process groups are killed on cancel and at app exit.
context: The user wanted an AI view of which big folders are safe to reclaim, built like two-edged sword's Ask: a model setting and a chat panel with suggested questions, default Opus, no API keys to manage.
decision: src-tauri/src/assistant.rs runs claude -p with stream-json, partial messages, --tools "" and --strict-mcp-config in the app data folder's claude/ subfolder, appending a disk-space-adviser system prompt; text deltas stream to the window as ask-chunk events and ask-done carries the session id, which a follow-up resumes. The first message of a chat (and any follow-up after the folder on screen changes) carries src/context.ts describeView: the volume, the folder on screen and its biggest folders nested three deep, folders under 0.5% folded. Models are Claude Code's opus/sonnet/haiku aliases (src/assistant.ts), default opus, remembered in localStorage askModel and chosen in the panel header since the app has no settings screen. The Ask button and panel are hidden when the CLI is not installed. Chats live in the panel's state only; the panel is hidden, not unmounted, when closed.
title: Ask runs the local Claude Code CLI with no tools, fed the scan as text

consequences: Any of four signed-in CLIs can answer; the status check runs agy models and four --version calls at launch, off the main thread. Codex answers arrive whole, not streamed. The code is a port of two-edged sword's GPL drivers by the same author, relicensed MIT here.
context: Ask first ran only Claude Code. The user wants the same CLI choice as two-edged sword, grouped by the tool that runs them, and a disabled Ask button that says why when nothing is installed, rather than a hidden one. Supersedes the Claude-only part of D-20261008-01.
decision: src-tauri/src/assistant/ is a module: mod.rs holds the shared prompt, process tracking, assistant_status (path, version and models per CLI) and the dispatch by model id prefix (agy:, copilot:, claude, else Codex); claude.rs, codex.rs, antigravity.rs and copilot.rs drive each CLI with the same flags as two-edged sword, minus every tool: Claude --tools "", Antigravity a per-run agent with tools: [], Copilot --available-tools=view in an empty folder (an empty list means every tool), Codex the read-only sandbox told to run nothing. Codex models come from its models_cache.json, Antigravity's from agy models, Copilot offers auto only. src/assistant.ts tags models by provider and groups them (Claude Code, ChatGPT (Codex), Antigravity (Google), GitHub Copilot) for the panel's optgroup select; pickModel falls back to the first offered model when the remembered one is gone. With no model anywhere the Ask button is disabled and its tooltip says to install a CLI, or to sign in when one is installed but lists no models. Each answer has a Copy button writing HTML from md.ts with the Markdown as the plain-text alternative, through the clipboard plugin's writeHtml (capability clipboard-manager:allow-write-html).
title: Ask supports Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and Copilot, all without tools; disabled with a reason when none offers a model

consequences: Every title in the app is now the custom tooltip, including ones set from DOM code (the treemap's reveal button) and truncated file names in the file table. Keep title text short: what it does, and its shortcut.
context: macOS's native tooltips look out of place beside the app's panels and can fall outside the window; the user asked for the app's own, positioned to stay on screen, as two-edged sword does.
decision: src/Tooltips.tsx is mounted once in App. Give an element a title (or an icon-only button an aria-label) and it gets the tooltip: on first hover the title moves to data-tip so the native one never shows. It is measured after render, then placed below the element centred on it, above when there is no room below, beside it when neither, and clamped inside the window with an 8px margin. Shown after 450ms on hover or keyboard focus; hidden on leaving, pressing, scrolling or resizing. A disabled button gets no pointer events in WebKit, so a tooltip that must show while disabled (the Ask button's reason) sits on a .tipwrap span around it. Do not build other tooltip components or rely on native ones.
title: Always use the app's own tooltip

consequences: A feature change means a guide edit, which updates the help and GitHub at once. The guide has no screenshots or external links; lines pointing at docs/ or screenshots/ are dropped when parsed. The app has no native menu bar, so there is no Help menu item.
context: The app had no user guide beyond the README and no help in the window. The user wants the help button and drawer two-edged sword has.
decision: docs/guide.md is the user guide and the only copy of the help text: src/guides.ts imports it raw at build time and splits it by ## into sections, with a Markdown renderer for paragraphs, lists, tables, quotes and in-guide links. src/Help.tsx is a drawer over the right of the map opened by the title bar's ? button or the ? key (with or without ⌘) outside a text box; Esc closes it; its box searches every section; its foot hands a question to Ask through App's askSeed state, which types it into Ask's box. Ask and Help share the right edge so opening one closes the other. The README links to the guide instead of repeating it.
title: In-app help drawer built from docs/guide.md

consequences: About a thousand more tokens per call. A guide edit changes what the model says about the app; keep those five sections accurate. Copilot still takes the prompt in its first user turn, so it stays the weakest.
context: Copilot explained the gap between the disk's used figure and the scan total as if the app were broken. The CLIs have no tools, so the facts have to be in the prompt.
decision: assistant::system() builds the system prompt once: SYSTEM, then the Map, Free space, Cloud folders, Scanning and Full Disk Access sections of docs/guide.md, included at compile time with include_str!. SYSTEM says the figures are measured facts, the gap is expected and explained by the guide, never to suggest the app is wrong, and to raise skipped folders only when asked or when it changes the advice, ending with the Full Disk Access step. The context's denied-folders line is neutral: skipped because unreadable; the sizes cover what could be read.
title: Ask's prompt carries the guide's sections on the app's figures, and treats them as facts

consequences: macOS treats it as a new app: Full Disk Access must be granted again and the first launch rescans. The set_process_name workaround in main.rs is gone because the binary and product names now match. The GitHub repo and local folder are still named disk-usage-visualiser until the app is published.
context: The app is growing from a disk-usage treemap into a disk and performance trend monitor, so 'Disk Usage' no longer describes it. Telltale, Lookout, Witness and Observer were rejected for clashes or being too generic.
decision: Rename in place to Tidemark (tagline: the high-water marks of your Mac): product, binary, crate, bundle id com.wayned.tidemark, data folder Application Support/Tidemark, DMG Tidemark.dmg, env var TIDEMARK_TIMING. No migration of the old data folder: the app had no real users yet.
title: Rename Disk Usage to Tidemark

consequences: No hourly rollup tier. Slow disk growth stays visible over a year at a cost of a few hundred KB; slow performance regressions older than 14 days are not visible. The collector runs from the tray app, so launch at login matters.
context: Tidemark tracks disk and performance over time. Hourly full disk scans are too costly (~30s of full CPU), and per-process performance data is the main source of volume. A year of detailed history is not needed; most questions are about the last day or week.
decision: One SQLite file (rusqlite, WAL) for all history. Performance: raw samples every 2-5s in memory only for live charts (~15 min); 1-minute rollups (min/avg/max, max never averaged away) kept 14 days; top 5-10 processes by CPU and memory per minute keyed by app name, plus an other bucket; threshold incidents stored with a detailed process snapshot. Read cumulative counters so averages stay exact at slower sampling. Disk: hourly statfs free-space samples; one full scan a day when idle and on power, FSEvents for incremental rescans; per snapshot store folders over ~100 MB or within 3-4 levels, kept 14 days. Plus one row per day of total disk use and top-folder sizes, kept a year. Sleep is a gap, not zeros. Settings: history length, disk scan frequency, launch at login.
title: History: 14 days detailed, daily disk totals for a year

consequences: New source files carry the GPL-3.0-or-later SPDX header. Releases after 2.0.0 are GPL; 2.0.0 and earlier were published under MIT.
context: Tidemark was MIT. Brainstead and two-edged sword, by the same author, are GPL, and Ask's CLI drivers were ported from two-edged sword's GPL code.
decision: LICENSE is the GNU GPL v3 text; every source header, package.json and Cargo.toml say GPL-3.0-or-later; the README says so.
title: Relicence Tidemark under the GPL, version 3 or later

consequences: History grows by two REAL columns a minute. Per-core history over time is not available; adding it later means a new table. The demo in tools/screenshots.py assumes efficiency cores are numbered first, as on every Apple Silicon Mac so far.
context: Showing per-core CPU means reading every core; keeping each core per minute in history would multiply the CPU data stored by 10-16 on an Apple Silicon Mac, while what a person looks back for is whether the performance or the efficiency cores were working.
decision: Each core's use is kept for the latest reading only (Live.cores, LiveInfo.core_use) and drawn on the Now CPU card behind a chevron. History keeps two columns a minute, cpu_p and cpu_e, the performance and efficiency cores' averages, drawn as extra lines on the Performance CPU chart. A core's kind comes from the device tree's cluster-type by logical-cpu-id, read once; where the Mac doesn't say (Intel) there is no split and the columns are unlabelled.
title: Per-core CPU: each core live only, the P/E split per minute

consequences: The headline, the tray's line and its one suggested action are still about the worst measure only. Status grows a list; older readers of the field ignore it.
context: The status named one measure, the worst, so a Mac with memory critical and the CPU busy showed only memory; the busy CPU card looked calm.
decision: status() collects every condition in its order of severity, keeps one per measure (the worst), and returns the first as the headline with the rest in Status.also. The screens colour each card from its own entry (statusFor/flagFor in src/status.ts), and Ask describes the flag of the card it was asked from.
title: The status flags every measure that needs attention, worst first

consequences: Details links open a tab (perfTabs.ts tabFor); a card's data-focus must be on the tab tabFor names. History's procs rows carry per-app peaks and disk, so they are larger. Old minutes have no per-app peaks; the snapshot shows their averages.
context: The sidebar read Now, Performance, Disk Map, Trends; Performance was one long page of every chart with its details mixed in, and its name didn't say which span of time it covers next to Now and Trends.
decision: The screen is called Recent (Now, Recent, Trends, Disk Map; ⌘1-⌘4) and has tabs: All, one equal-height chart per measure with no details, and CPU, GPU, Memory, Disk I/O, Network, Energy, each with its parts, busiest apps, incidents and busiest moments. The internal id stays performance (Performance.tsx, screenshot names, the site's #performance anchor). The snapshot follows whichever chart is clicked, leads with the average the line shows, and lists apps by their average, their peak (history keeps each app's peak per minute) or an incident's own snapshot, saying which.
title: Performance becomes Recent, with a tab per measure

consequences: Login Items lists the helper by its program (a generic icon), not as part of Tidemark.app. Signing with a Developer ID (a team ID) would let SMAppService work again, as one Login Items entry; that is the proper fix if the app is published.
context: SMAppService registration of the helper never ran for an app signed with a self-signed identity: Background Task Management allowed no build (OS_REASON_CODESIGNING). The app has no users yet besides its developer.
decision: The app writes com.wayned.tidemark.helper.plist in the user's LaunchAgents folder pointing at the installed binary and loads it with launchctl; Settings reads it as on only when it is loaded and not disabled; the app reloads it at launch when moved or rebuilt, never when switched off in Login Items. The bundled SMAppService plist and the code moving installs off it are removed outright rather than kept for a migration.
title: The background helper is a plain LaunchAgent, until the app has a Developer ID

consequences: Trends fills in a day at a time and says how far back it goes. A day's apps are averaged over the minutes each ran. The heatmap still comes from the minutes, so it covers 14 days whatever the range.
context: Recent now covers every measure from an hour to 14 days, and per-minute history is kept 14 days at most; Trends was disk space over 7 days to a year, a CPU heatmap and a row of highs, which by then repeated Recent.
decision: history keeps perf_daily: one row per local day rolled up from the minutes (averages and peaks, bytes read/written/downloaded/uploaded, watt-hours, incident and crash counts, the day's busiest apps as JSON), refreshed every ten minutes for today and yesterday, backfilled for any day still in the minutes, rolled up before pruning, kept 366 days. Trends shows 30 days, 3 months or 12 months with Recent's tabs, one chart per measure (the day's figure as the line, its peak as the band), a card for the picked or busiest day with its apps, each tab's records and a by-hour heatmap of its measure; Disk space keeps the projection and folders that rose.
title: Trends is every measure a day at a time, from a daily row kept for a year

consequences: A feature change means editing the matching src/help page, and docs/ or the site where they cover it too: the three are separate copies now and can drift. Because Ask treats the help as fact, its accuracy matters more than the docs'.
context: D-20261008-04 made docs/guide.md the only copy of the help text. The guide has since been split into short pages per screen, and the repo docs (README, docs/) became a separate, briefer set for GitHub.
decision: The help text lives in src/help/*.md, one short page per screen or topic. src/guides.ts imports them raw at build time, in the order the app presents them, and splits each by ## into sections the drawer (src/Help.tsx) can open and search; intro.md carries the title. The drawer opens from the title bar's ? button or the ? key, Esc closes it, and its foot hands a question to Ask. Ask's prompt carries these pages' sections on the app's figures as facts.
title: In-app help drawer built from src/help/*.md

consequences: No disk writes for live readings; readings arrive as they are taken; the app takes over at once when the helper's connection drops. The recorder removes live.json and the old marker files when it starts serving. A socket path over 104 bytes would fail to bind, and the app would then show no live readings while the helper records.
context: When the background helper records, the app needs its live readings. They were shared by rewriting live.json every 2-5 s, about 1 GB of physical writes a day even after trimming, with marker files (following, watching) to say whether anyone was reading and whether a window was on screen.
decision: The recorder serves live.sock in the data folder; a follower connects, gets one line of JSON per sample (in full while it has a window on screen, else the latest reading and busiest apps) and says 1 or 0 down the same stream when its window appears or goes. The connection's presence replaces the marker files. Writes have a 1 s timeout and a stuck follower is dropped; SO_NOSIGPIPE keeps a vanished one from killing the recorder.
title: Live readings go to the app over a Unix socket

consequences: The helper is down only for the swap and comes back on the new build, so the restarted app's refresh() finds its build current. If the reload fails the helper stays off until Settings turns it on again, since refresh() only reloads a loaded agent.
context: The updater swaps /Applications/Tidemark.app, which the launchd helper (Tidemark --record) also runs from; make install-app boots the helper out first and loads it again after. AppHandle::restart skips RunEvent::Exit when called on the main thread.
decision: updates.rs downloads first, then recorder::stop_for_update (bootout, only when the agent runs this binary and is loaded), Update::install, recorder::start_after_update (install(), from the new binary), then AppHandle::request_restart so the normal quit work runs. busy() postpones the install during a scan (the app's, or any holder of the scan lock) or while Ask is answering.
title: In-app updates stop and restart the background helper around the bundle swap
